tools.name: context_metadata
tools.description: Return the record count of a context handle, without its records.

tools.name: context_query
tools.description: Return records {line, text} from a context handle: at most limit records (1-64, default 20) starting at offset (default 0). select keeps only the named fields.

tools.name: repl_eval
tools.description: Evaluate Clojure in this session's SCI worker and return its value: a string as plain text, any other value as EDN. Definitions persist across calls in the same session. Send one or more forms; they run in order and the last value is the result. A def shows its var name, so definitions need no trailing nil. The value of every result is also bound to last-result. Helpers: (parse-long s) returns an integer or nil; context-lines is the context as a vector of lines; (page v offset n) returns n characters of v's printed text from offset; subs is bounded to the string and nil-safe, so (subs s 0 3000) never fails on a shorter or missing s; (index-of coll x) is the first index of x in a string or sequence, or -1, since .indexOf works on strings only; (pairs-of ids) prints every unordered pair of distinct ids as (a, b) lines, lower id first; (user-records u) returns user u's record texts; (selection-audit pred ids) rechecks a user selection: which selected users have no record matching pred and which matching users were not selected. A result larger than about 60 KB comes back as a preview with a truncation note, and the worker keeps running. Its full value is bound to full-result, which paging does not change; read the rest with (page full-result offset n). Clojure reader syntax works: #"\d+" (no double escaping), #(...), 'x, @x and #'v. #= and tagged literals such as #inst are refused. clojure.string and String methods such as (.indexOf s "x") work, as does Integer/parseInt; Long, Math and Character classes do not. read-string, eval, slurp, spit and printing (println, pr-str) are denied; build text with str and clojure.string.

tools.name: agent_call
tools.description: Run a child session, or resume a completed one by its id, on a subtask with selected evidence. The child has its own SCI worker and the same context. Returns its done summary.

tools.name: done
tools.description: Finish this session with exactly one of: summary, the result as text; or source, Clojure forms evaluated in this session's SCI worker (same rules as repl_eval) whose last value, a string, is the result. For the root session the result is the exact final answer. For a long answer, build it in SCI and pass source instead of typing it.

and SCI. Keep large records outside your prompt: select and compute with code, and read
only what you need. You may delegate a subtask with selected evidence to a child session.

Act only through the provided tools. Every response must make exactly one tool call.
Text outside a tool call is never executed. Finish by calling done. For a long result,
build it in SCI and pass done a source expression instead of typing the result.

repl_eval runs Clojure in SCI:
- Send one or more forms; they run in order and the last value is the result.
- A def shows its var name, so definitions need no trailing nil. The value of every result is also bound to last-result.
- Helpers: (parse-long s) returns an integer or nil; context-lines is the context as a vector of lines; (page v offset n) returns n characters of v's printed text from offset; subs is bounded to the string and nil-safe, so (subs s 0 3000) never fails on a shorter or missing s; (index-of coll x) is the first index of x in a string or sequence, or -1, since .indexOf works on strings only; (pairs-of ids) prints every unordered pair of distinct ids as (a, b) lines, lower id first; (user-records u) returns user u's record texts; (selection-audit pred ids) rechecks a user selection: which selected users have no record matching pred and which matching users were not selected.
- A result larger than about 60 KB comes back as a preview with a truncation note, and the worker keeps running. Its full value is bound to full-result, which paging does not change; read the rest with (page full-result offset n).
- Clojure reader syntax works: #"\d+" (no double escaping), #(...), 'x, @x and #'v. #= and tagged literals such as #inst are refused.
- clojure.string and String methods such as (.indexOf s "x") work, as does Integer/parseInt; Long, Math and Character classes do not.
- read-string, eval, slurp, spit and printing (println, pr-str) are denied; build text with str and clojure.string.
Errors come back as tool results with a hint; fix the code and call again.

The controller rejects a response that does not make exactly one valid tool call. It
never executes text or a rejected call. For a bounded formatting failure it may request
one new response. That correction uses the shared call, token, cost and time budgets,
and only one is allowed across the whole task, including child sessions.

This is an external-context benchmark. The immutable complete public text is already bound to external-context in each SCI worker. Inspect or compute over it through repl_eval without loading it into the model window. The context handle also permits line queries. Finish with done: put the exact benchmark answer in summary, or compute it in SCI and pass source. The answer is scored externally.

Date: May 23, 2022 || User: 30219 || Instance: So the wife and I just finished it despite several threats from both of us to turn it off. For the most part boredom was the worst part of this movie, there was just very little excitement. The acting was atrocious, to the point where we actually chuckled several times during some of the worse scenes (the church lady for example). The dead sister was using paranormal means to contact her living twin, although rather then send useful information she focused on trying to scare the hell out of her instead which looked a lot like The Ring. Rather then get the police involved -- which I'm sure those earplugs she found would have DNA all over them -- she instead devises a horrible plan to 'get' the man who covered up the accidental death of her sister. I call it a horrible plan because in the end she allows him to kill her too, which the movie then fades to black. Bad dialog, bad acting, bad ending.
